title: Red-team spec RT1-RT12 as executable test plan
outcome: Sprint 4 test spec: each of RT1-RT12 written so an engineer can turn it into a pytest or live demo script without asking
acceptance: Each RT has: setup (seed, agents, preconditions), script outline (steps the rogue code runs), observable signal, binary pass criterion, owner module
Pass criteria are machine-checkable (exit code, record field, count == 0), not prose
Marks which run live at finale (F5/F6, ks inject, DB bypass, line edit, full rewrite) vs pytest-only (F3), per D11
RT11 scores false-positive cost; RT3 asserts the claimed agent is NOT suspended (D7 anti-framing)

summary: tests/redteam/SPEC.md: RT1-RT12 each with setup, rogue script outline, signal, binary pass expression over the C6 run dir / ks verify exit enum / counts, owner modules + ADR. LIVE at finale: RT1 DB bypass, RT3 forgery (F5), RT7 line edit and RT8 full rewrite (F6), RT10 F2+ via ks inject with hold 0 vs >0; F3 is a pytest-only variant of RT10; the rest are pytest and the jury may try them through the template. RT3 asserts billing stays active and only conn:R is suspended; RT11 asserts suspend-not-revoke, release restores the victim, and fp_cost is recomputed independently. Section 3 defines the jury rogue template (ctx.send/raw_send/sign_envelope/reconnect/report/dump, ks run --rogue). 10 contract requests Q1-Q10 for CON-01/SEC-03, the big one being Q9: C2 has no agent_id/act_chain. Open D7 point: an unattributable DB bypass suspends nobody. RT2 note: the container is uid 0, so agents can be dropped to a separate uid, which may make key isolation enforceable here.
